answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an AI-agent economy can enforce slashable staking at its network wharf, maintaining a protected oasis of verified peers. Each agent must deposit scarce capital into escrow to participate; detected fraud triggers immediate bond forfeiture. An attacker incurs a direct financial cost per identity, making large-scale forgery prohibitively expensive. Discarding ivory tower assumptions of trust, this design deters clones but unfairly marginalizes capital-poor agents.
